A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedDRM work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10/20/100 experiments, baseline comparisons, and sensitivity analyses in Section 3 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the CIFAR experiments and adds original RETINA medical-image results and a Dirichlet label-shift sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, personalized target heads, shared client classifier, weighted two-cross-entropy objective, federated updates, and maximum-probability routing remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is reformatted, and the existing reweighting strategy receives greater emphasis without a new procedural component.

E1.justification: Section 4 adds RETINA binary glaucoma classification using ACRIMA, Rim, and Refuge as three clients. This extends evaluation from CIFAR object classification with simulated heterogeneity to medical images with naturally differing clinical-source distributions. Existing CIFAR coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same ten baselines, and Table 3 retains FedAS and FedAvgFT. The new RETINA comparison and label-shift sweep reuse the existing ten-method comparator set; no evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated fine-tuning allocation from 100 local steps to 100 local rounds after 700 global rounds; this is a substantive reported budget revision, without evidence establishing reruns. RETINA introduces 96×96 inputs, 4608/512 embedding/projection dimensions, batch size 32, and 100 rounds with a 90/10 global/local allocation. Appendix F.2.4 adds a controlled Dirichlet-parameter sweep.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2.4 adds a focused label-shift sensitivity analysis at Dirichlet parameters 0.3, 1.3, and 2.3, testing effects on local and system accuracy. Figure 7 additionally examines medical-task training-loss trajectories. Existing loss-weight, covariate-shift, client-count, and backbone-sharing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over the final 50 communication rounds, and Table 4 follows the existing numerical reporting convention. No independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added.

E6.justification: New results include RETINA accuracy and loss comparisons in Figure 7 and the label-shift sweep in Table 4. Table 1 also revises FedDRM's Dir-0.3 system accuracies from 63.85 to 62.78, 37.67 to 37.63, and 26.01 to 26.03 for CIFAR-10/20/100; Table 2 changes CIFAR-10 average accuracy from 80.25 to 80.26, with accompanying standard-deviation changes. Table 4 nevertheless retains v1's CIFAR-10 values at parameter 0.3, leaving an unexplained disagreement with the revised main tables.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.2 explicitly adds the qualification 'For any fixed θ' while retaining optimality. Equation (3) also changes its printed ratio from dP_1^(i)/dP_1^(0) to dP_k^(i)/dP_1^(i), inconsistently with the surrounding reference-distribution description and retained Appendix C.1 derivation. These are localized changes; the remaining theoretical results and proofs are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly identifies the existing reweighting correction as a separate main contribution and refines the novelty claim to the first statistically grounded joint prediction-and-routing framework. The central claims about exploiting heterogeneity, routing queries, and improving predictive performance remain.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2.4 adds a substantive explanation that stronger label skew can simplify local classification while undermining agreement among personalized models used for majority voting. Section 4 interprets RETINA results as evidence of practical robustness to simultaneous shifts. Existing qualifications about severe distribution differences and scalability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new medical experiment documents source datasets, exclusion of Drishti, image dimensions, class ratios, embedding and projection dimensions, batch size, and training allocations. The label-shift sweep specifies its parameter values. These extend reproducibility information for the added experiments; the code-access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds explicit links to earlier density-ratio and empirical-likelihood research, including Kay and Little, Qin and Zhang, and Chen and Liu. Medical-dataset and LeNet references are also added. The existing discussion of aggregation, personalization, and clustering retains its basic positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction's motivation and contribution paragraphs are rewritten, DRM/EL explanations gain connecting prose, and terminology is refined. A medical-experiment section and label-shift appendix subsection are inserted, alongside affiliation and acknowledgment edits. Most retained sections preserve their wording and narrative order.

P2.justification: The document is reset throughout in ICLR conference formatting, changing typography, margins, headers, spacing, and float placement. New displays comprise the RETINA accuracy/loss panels in Figure 7, label-distribution panels in Figure 14, and Table 4. Existing visual content is largely retained, with expanded captions and v1 Figures 7–12 renumbered as v2 Figures 8–13.

improvement.justification: RETINA provides useful evidence beyond v1's simulated CIFAR heterogeneity, directly supporting the motivating medical application. The added label-shift analysis also improves understanding of the evaluation metrics. These gains are moderated by the new Equation (3) inconsistency and unreconciled CIFAR-10 values between Tables 1–2 and Table 4, yielding a limited overall improvement.
